lessons.lesson: Review every held position on every run, including days with no trade: distance from price to the invalidation, earnings dates now inside the 5-day window versus what the thesis says, and thesis text that has gone stale. Where an invalidation clause is qualitative (e.g. 'exchange failure'), state in the reasoning whether it has tripped, and why. Write the re-anchored level or date into the decision reasoning rather than only flagging it. When a held name gaps far from the price its stop was written against, re-anchor the stop to the close and to the gain, and name any stop within about 2% of the market together with the dated catalysts. Compute every stop distance and position weight from the latest mark in the inputs, say which mark was used, and after a large up day restate the dollar risk of a held-through-earnings position at its current weight. When a stop is re-anchored after a big run-up, or a stop or the SPY 200-day line is within about 10% of the mark, also state the distance on a mark 4-5% lower, since the inputs are pre-open and the day can move that far. Do not write weight or return-on-cost figures into stored thesis text; they go stale overnight.
evidence: 2026-10-30 IDXX: the 10-20 thesis says earnings (11-02) are outside the 5-day window; the print is now one trading day out, the position fell 4.3% today with no news, and only the Skeptic's objection and the News Analyst's upcoming note brought the stale premise up. The PM did weigh it (stress loss about $3) and held knowingly; the thesis text is still stale.
